tb21_profile.skill: Non-linear least-squares fitting of overlapping Lorentzian peaks (x0, gamma, amplitude, offset) to a noisy 1D spectrum and emitting the parameters as structured JSON
tb21_profile.domain: Numerical/scientific Python: numpy + scipy.optimize curve fitting, Raman/vibrational spectroscopy of graphene (G and 2D bands)
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec: read a data file, model it, write a fixed-schema JSON result that is checked numerically

verifier_notes: The packet's `verifier` field and work/verifier_strength.json disagree for several CalibForge ids; verifier_strength.json is the newer file (23:01 vs the 22:56 packet) and I trusted it after reading the tests. scientific-computing_20260415_123352_007 is shown as `weak` in the packet but its tests/test_outputs.py holds the 5 true Lorentzian parameters and asserts peak positions within 10 cm^-1, >=4/5 centres within 5 cm^-1 and gamma/amplitude within a factor of 3 - verifier_strength.json grades it strong/0.875, which is right. Same direction for scientific-computing_20260416_031414_007 and scientific-computing_20260508_045557_007 (packet weak/ok, file strong). scientific-computing_20260504_125558_004 is a near-perfect Raman/fluorescence-baseline match but FREE in both sources, so it is out of final_top10 and out of per_source. task_001144_e1380e49 (multi-Lorentzian PSD fit) is a strong skill match but FREE, likewise excluded. Note work/free_verifier_tasks.tsv is NOT a FREE list - it lists any task with a cheap assertion, including strong ones - do not use it as the gate.

notes: CalibForge is a genuine and large upgrade here: it supplies six of the final ten, including two real Raman tasks and one whose results.json schema (x0/gamma/amplitude per Lorentzian) is the TB2.1 schema. Before v2 the best available were TMax's task_005968_01db9842 and task_000242_341bf3b8, which are still strong, so CalibForge beats but does not replace TMax. Terminal-Lego contributes nothing to the top ten: its curve-fitting tasks are toy-scale (fit a quadratic to four points) and the corpus was only reachable by grepping /data/yichuan_wang/terminal-lego-15k (tools.py does not index it); task_04540, task_13601, task_04622 and task_12877 came from that grep rather than the packet. Recursive-Task-Synthesis and TerminalWorld genuinely have fewer than 10 defensible candidates - `search rts "Lorentzian|curve_fit|spectr|gaussian"` returns zero hits and `search tw` for the same returns two irrelevant ones - so their lists are filled with generic numeric-analysis chores scored 1-2 and should be ignored downstream. SWE-Smith likewise has no fitting content; only dask lstsq is defensible. Two excellent skill matches were excluded from final_top10 for the FREE rule: scientific-computing_20260504_125558_004 (Raman fluorescence-baseline removal plus peak fitting) and task_001144_e1380e49 (multi-Lorentzian PSD fit). If the FREE rule is ever relaxed for a task with a repairable verifier, those two are the first to reconsider.
